instrument.name: IPIP character scales
instrument.author: International Personality Item Pool (ipip.ori.org): ten of the preliminary IPIP scales measuring constructs similar to those in Cloninger's Temperament and Character Inventory
instrument.licence: The IPIP items are in the public domain.
instrument.prompt: Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Read each statement and choose how accurately it describes you.
instrument.norms: There is no reference group. The IPIP publishes no norms for these scales, so a score is read off the five-point scale itself: the average answer, after reversing the statements keyed the other way. Below 3.0 is low and above 4.0 is high.

dimensions.name: Self-Directedness
dimensions.about: Cloninger's measure of self-mastery: taking charge of your own life, and acting from purposes you have chosen.
dimensions.low: The answers describe less self-mastery than most would want: direction, follow-through or contentment are often out of reach.
dimensions.typical: The answers describe a fair measure of self-mastery, with some areas that give way under pressure.
dimensions.high: The answers describe a person largely in charge of their own life, working from purposes they have chosen.

dimensions.name: Cooperativeness
dimensions.about: Cloninger's measure of how far you see yourself as part of humanity: conscience, forgiveness and regard for others.
dimensions.low: The answers describe someone guarded towards others, keeping account of what is owed.
dimensions.typical: The answers describe ordinary decency and goodwill, within limits.
dimensions.high: The answers describe warmth, conscience and an easy readiness to forgive.

dimensions.name: Self-Transcendence
dimensions.about: Cloninger's measure of feeling part of something larger: absorption, imagination and a sense of meaning.
dimensions.low: The answers keep to what can be seen and counted.
dimensions.typical: The answers leave room for imagination and meaning without living there.
dimensions.high: The answers describe a person often absorbed, and moved by a sense of something larger.

scales.name: Satisfaction
scales.measures: Being at ease in your own life, against feeling short-changed, attacked or used.
scales.low: Often feels hard done by, wary of other people's motives, and short of pleasure.
scales.typical: Content enough on the whole, with some sore points.
scales.high: Largely at ease with life, and not looking for slights.

scales.name: Optimism
scales.measures: Knowing what you want and believing your efforts count, against drifting or feeling fated.
scales.low: Unsure where life is going, and apt to let others or fate decide.
scales.typical: Has a working sense of direction, which comes and goes.
scales.high: Knows what is wanted, keeps improving, and does not give up hope.

scales.name: Resourcefulness
scales.measures: Meeting problems directly, against being discouraged or waiting for a lead.
scales.low: Easily discouraged or intimidated, and slow to decide.
scales.typical: Copes with most problems, and sometimes wants a lead.
scales.high: Faces problems directly and expects to deal with them.

scales.name: Self-Acceptance
scales.measures: Taking yourself as you are, against needing status, advantage or someone to look down on.
scales.low: Much taken up with status and with comparing oneself to others.
scales.typical: Mostly settled, with some wish to measure up.
scales.high: Has little need to compete or to impress.

scales.name: Impulse Control
scales.measures: Doing what you meant to do, against acting in ways you later regret.
scales.low: Often does things later regretted, and loses time and chances.
scales.typical: Carries out most plans, with lapses.
scales.high: Follows through, and resists what would get in the way.

scales.name: Empathy
scales.measures: Sensing what others feel and acting on it.
scales.low: Other people's feelings and needs are not much attended to.
scales.typical: Notices others' feelings and looks after them when it occurs.
scales.high: Picks up what others feel and takes time for them.

scales.name: Compassion
scales.measures: Forgiving and accepting weakness, against holding grudges and getting even.
scales.low: Holds on to injuries, and may want to get even.
scales.high: Lets injuries go, and accepts others' weaknesses.

scales.name: Morality
scales.measures: Following conscience, against deceit and misuse of power.
scales.low: Treats conscience as negotiable when the end seems to justify it.
scales.typical: Means to do right, and usually does.
scales.high: Goes by conscience, and stands behind what is done.

scales.name: Imagination
scales.measures: Absorption, fantasy and being carried away, against keeping to what is literal.
scales.low: Keeps to the literal and the by-the-book.
scales.typical: Has some inner life and some taste for the strange.
scales.high: Easily absorbed, and lives a good deal in imagination.

scales.name: Romanticism
scales.measures: Finding beauty, passion and meaning in things, against seeing nothing beyond them.
scales.low: Looks for little beyond the plain fact of things.
scales.typical: Finds meaning in some things and not in others.
scales.high: Moved by beauty and meaning, and passionate about what is taken up.

items.text: Get so involved with things that I forget the time.
See beauty in things that others might not notice.
Am able to control my cravings.
Feel that my life lacks direction.
Wait for others to lead the way.
Rarely look for a deeper meaning in things.
Am out for my own personal gain.
Don't know why I do some of the things I do.
Feel that people have a hard time understanding me.
Like to get lost in thought.
Am not sure where my life is going.
See other people as my competitors.
Believe that the end justifies the means.
Am inexplicably happy some of the time.
Am not in the mood for anything.
Have a good word for everyone.
Am not interested in abstract ideas.
Find it hard to forgive others.
Do things that others find strange.
Enjoy examining myself and my life.
Return extra change when a cashier makes a mistake.
Am embarrassed to have people see my home.
Am passionate about anything I'm involved in.
Do the opposite of what is asked.
